newsitem.title: USA: Global computer chip sales off 2.4 pct in Feb - SIA.
newsitem.headline: Global computer chip sales off 2.4 pct in Feb - SIA.

text.p: Worldwide computer chip sales in February fell 2.4 percent to $10.4 billion from $10.65 billion the previous month, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association's Global Billings Report.
The largest drop was in Japan, where sales fell 4.4 percent to $2.57 billion from $2.69 billion in January.
However, the yen declined 3.1 percent against the dollar in February, making that month's decline in the value of chip sales only 1.3 percent in terms of the Japanese currency, the report said.
Total February sales, compiled by the 70-member World Semiconductor Trade Statistics organization, fell 15.5 percent from February 1996 billings of $12.3 billion.
In North and South America, billings in February 1997 approached $3.41 billion, a 0.6 percent drop from January sales of $3.43 billion.
In the Asia-Pacific market, sales reached $2.17 billion, a 3.9 percent drop from January sales of $2.25 billion.
In Europe, sales dropped 1.1 percent to $2.24 billion from $2.27 billion.
